subject.title: Fix Claude never-prompt no-UI Keychain repair for missing credentials file (#1975)

question: Should Claude never-prompt mode forbid only interactive Keychain UI, allowing fail-closed Security.framework no-UI reads, or should it forbid every read of the Claude Code Keychain item?
rationale: Both interpretations are defensible security contracts, and changing the established meaning of a credential-access preference requires explicit maintainer intent rather than an automated code judgment.

options.title: Allow no-UI reads
options.body: Treat `.never` as a no-prompt policy, allow only fail-closed no-UI reads, and retain Advanced → Disable Keychain access as the absolute opt-out.

options.title: Forbid all reads
options.body: Keep `.never` as a complete Claude Code Keychain block and solve missing-file recovery through a different source or explicit user action.

options.title: Add a separate mode
options.body: Preserve the current strict interpretation and introduce a distinct preference for silent no-UI recovery, accepting additional configuration complexity.

recommendation.title: Allow no-UI reads
recommendation.body: Treat `.never` as a no-prompt policy, allow only fail-closed no-UI reads, and retain Advanced → Disable Keychain access as the absolute opt-out.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a user-facing security and preference-contract choice for the repository rather than a mechanical implementation detail.
